title: Principalization of an ideal supported at finitely many regular surface points
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact (every open cover has a finite subcover). Let $T\subseteq X$ be a finite set of closed points such that $\mathcal O_{X,p}$ is a regular local ring of Krull dimension $2$ for every $p\in T$ [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Let $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ be a quasi-coherent ideal [pqf-def-coherent] such that $(\mathcal O_X/\mathcal I)_x=0$ for every $x\notin T$. There exist $n\geq0$ and a sequence $X_n\xrightarrow{b_n}\cdots\xrightarrow{b_1}X_0=X$ such that each $b_{i+1}$ is the blowup [def-nagata-global-blowup] in the reduced closed subscheme consisting of one closed point $p_i\in X_i$ whose image in $X$ belongs to $T$, and, for the composite $t:X_n\to X$, the extended ideal $\mathcal I\mathcal O_{X_n}$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal] is an effective Cartier ideal [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal], that is, locally generated by a nonzerodivisor, and is an invertible $\mathcal O_{X_n}$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. The length-zero sequence is permitted.

source.place: Tag 0AHH, resolve-lemma-make-ideal-principal; effective Cartier property in the final paragraph of its proof.

proof.text: For each $p\in T$, put $\ell_p=\operatorname{length}_{\mathcal O_{X,p}}(\mathcal O_{X,p}/\mathcal I_p)$. The quotient is cyclic and its support in the spectrum of the stalk is contained in the maximal ideal: its other points correspond to proper generizations of $p$, which cannot belong to the finite set of closed points $T$. The finite-length criterion [lem-sc-generic-stalk-finite-length] applies when this quotient is nonzero; a zero quotient has length zero. Thus $N=\sum_{p\in T}\ell_p$ is a natural number. Prove the assertion simultaneously for all the stated triples $(X,T,\mathcal I)$ by strong induction on $N$.

source.place: Tag 0AHH, proof, first paragraph: finite colengths and induction on their sum.

proof.text: If $N=0$, every quotient stalk at $T$ is zero (a nonzero module has the strict submodule chain $0\subsetneq M$). Every stalk outside $T$ is zero by hypothesis. Hence $\mathcal I=\mathcal O_X$. Its generator $1$ is a nonzerodivisor, so the length-zero sequence satisfies the effective Cartier and invertibility conclusions.

source.place: Tag 0AHH, proof, first paragraph: the zero case.

proof.text: If $N>0$, choose $p\in T$ with $\ell_p>0$ and blow up its reduced closed subscheme, writing $b:X'\to X$. On a Noetherian affine cover, the centre ideal is finitely generated by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]; the associated ideal sheaf is therefore of finite type by [pqf-def-coherent]. By [lemma-nagata-blowup-proper] the morphism is proper, hence of finite type, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X'$ Noetherian. By [thm-nagata-blowup-principalizes-center], the extended centre ideal $\mathcal L\subseteq\mathcal O_{X'}$ is effective Cartier. It cuts out the scheme-theoretic fibre $E=b^{-1}(p)$, and [thm-nagata-global-blowup-complement] identifies $X'\setminus E$ with $X\setminus\{p\}$.

source.place: Tag 0AHH, proof, second paragraph: blow up one point; preliminary discussion before the lemma.

proof.text: Put $A=\mathcal O_{X,p}$ and $I=\mathcal I_p$. The morphism $\operatorname{Spec}A\to X$ is flat by [lem-sbc-canonical-stalk-spectrum-flat]. Use the comparison for this flat map and the reduced-point ideal in [def-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change-map]. Its invertibility [thm-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change] therefore identifies $Y=X'\times_X\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathfrak m_A}(\operatorname{Spec}A)$; the pulled-back reduced centre is cut out by $\mathfrak m_A$. The exceptional fibre $E_Y$ is identified with $E$, since both are the base change to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(p)$. Apply [lem-sfb-local-surface-maximal-blowup-geometry] to $A$: $E_Y$ is a projective line, and its closed points have regular local rings of dimension $2$ on $Y$.

source.place: Tag 0AHH, proof, cartesian square and its exceptional divisors; local regularity input from Tag 0AGR.

proof.text: The ideal $I$ is proper because $\ell_p>0$, and its quotient has finite length by step 1. Apply [lem-sfb-local-surface-weak-transform-colength-drop]. It gives $d\geq1$, $I\mathcal O_Y\subseteq\mathcal O_Y(-dE_Y)$ and the residual ideal $\mathcal J_Y=I\mathcal O_Y(dE_Y)$. Its quotient is supported on finitely many closed points $S\subset E_Y$, with total local length strictly less than $\ell_p$.

source.place: Tag 0AHH, proof, application of Tag 0AGT to the chosen stalk ideal.

proof.text: Here is the global ideal inclusion omitted in the source. On affine rings $R\to B$, the inverse image of a closed subscheme $\operatorname{Spec}(R/K)$ has coordinate ring $B/KB$ (the quotient universal property). Thus the kernel definition of extended ideal is precisely $KB$. Choose an affine neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $p$, with prime $\mathfrak m$, and an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}B\subset b^{-1}(\operatorname{Spec}R)$. For a point $q\in E$ in this open, with prime $Q\subset B$, one has $Q\cap R=\mathfrak m$. Set $W=R\setminus\mathfrak m$. The corresponding affine base change is $\operatorname{Spec}(W^{-1}B)$, and $B_Q\cong(W^{-1}B)_{W^{-1}Q}$: every element of $W$ is already a unit in $B_Q$, and both maps send a fraction to the same fraction. The extended ideals of $\mathcal I$ and of the centre agree under this identification. Thus the local inclusion of step 5 gives $\mathcal I\mathcal O_{X',q}\subseteq\mathcal L_q^d$ at every $q\in E$. Off $E$ the right side is the unit ideal. Stalkwise inclusion gives $\mathcal I\mathcal O_{X'}\subseteq\mathcal L^d$. Locally choose a nonzerodivisor generator $e$ for $\mathcal L$ and set $\mathcal J=e^{-d}(\mathcal I\mathcal O_{X'})\subseteq\mathcal O_{X'}$. Changing $e$ by a unit changes this ideal by that unit's inverse $d$th power, so the local ideals agree and glue. They are quasi-coherent, and $\mathcal I\mathcal O_{X'}=\mathcal L^d\mathcal J$.

source.place: Tag 0AHH, proof, the inclusion marked "some details omitted" and the definition of the residual ideal.

proof.text: The stalk identifications of step 6 identify $\mathcal J$ on $E$ with $\mathcal J_Y$, and preserve the lengths of its stalk quotients. Off $E$ the factor $\mathcal L$ is the unit ideal, so $\mathcal J$ agrees with $\mathcal I$ under $X'\setminus E\cong X\setminus\{p\}$. Let $T'$ consist of the points corresponding to $S$ and the unique lifts of $T\setminus\{p\}$. These are closed in $X'$: the first set is closed in the closed fibre $E$, and each of the other points is the entire fibre over its closed image. Their local rings are regular of dimension $2$, by steps 4 and 6 on $E$ and the complement isomorphism elsewhere. The quotient $\mathcal O_{X'}/\mathcal J$ is supported in $T'$, and $$\sum_{q\in T'}\operatorname{length}_{\mathcal O_{X',q}}(\mathcal O_{X',q}/\mathcal J_q)<\ell_p+\sum_{t\in T\setminus\{p\}}\ell_t=N.$$ This uses the unweighted local-length inequality of step 5, so no equality of residue fields is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0AHH, proof, finite residual support and decrease of the sum of lengths.

proof.text: Apply the strong induction hypothesis to $(X',T',\mathcal J)$, which satisfies every hypothesis by steps 3 and 7 and has strictly smaller invariant. It gives a finite tower $h:Z\to X'$ of blowups at reduced closed points over $T'$ such that $\mathcal J\mathcal O_Z$ is effective Cartier. Every point of $T'$ maps into $T$. Prepending $b$ therefore gives a finite tower whose centres all map into the original $T$.

source.place: Tag 0AHH, proof, last paragraph: induction for the residual ideal.

proof.text: Apply [lemma-nagata-cartier-total-transform-blowup] successively along the finite tower $h$ to the effective Cartier ideal $\mathcal L$. Its extension $\mathcal L\mathcal O_Z$ remains effective Cartier. Extension of the identity in step 6 yields $$\mathcal I\mathcal O_Z=(\mathcal L\mathcal O_Z)^d(\mathcal J\mathcal O_Z).$$ Locally the right side is generated by $a^dc$, where $a$ and $c$ are nonzerodivisors. If $a^dcx=0$, repeated cancellation gives $x=0$. Thus $\mathcal I\mathcal O_Z$ is effective Cartier; multiplication by $a^dc$ identifies its local module with $\mathcal O_Z$, so it is invertible. This closes the induction.

source.place: Tag 0AHH, proof, last paragraph; divisors.tex Tag 0809 (divisors-lemma-blow-up-pullback-effective-Cartier); the product calculation is the elementary proof of Tag 01WU (divisors-lemma-sum-effective-Cartier-divisors).
